jurisdiction.name: Greece
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Greece regulates AI mainly through Law 5321/2026, which implements the EU AI Act and replaced the AI chapter of Law 4961/2022: it makes the data protection authority (HDPA) the main market surveillance authority and single point of contact, makes the telecoms regulator (EETT) the notifying authority and operator of an AI sandbox, and requires a register of AI systems used by public bodies. Policy is steered by the Ministry of Digital Governance's Special Secretariat for AI and Data Governance (2025) and the 2024 Blueprint for Greece's AI Transformation from the High-Level Advisory Committee on AI; a 2025 law created the Greek AI Factory, and 2026 rules govern AI in secondary schools and public-sector use of EU AI tools. The HDPA fined Clearview AI EUR 20 million in 2022.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Not yet verified from the official text: the AI law's parliamentary and consultation dates. Its implementing decisions are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Νόμος 5321/2026 - Μέτρα εφαρμογής του Κανονισμού (ΕΕ) 2024/1689 του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου και του Συμβουλίου της 13ης Ιουνίου 2024 (Κανονισμός για την τεχνητή νοημοσύνη) - Τροποποίηση του ν. 4961/2022 (Α΄146) και άλλες διατάξεις
instruments.english_title: Law 5321/2026 - Measures implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of 13 June 2024 (Artificial Intelligence Act) - Amendment of Law 4961/2022 and other provisions
instruments.issuing_authority: Hellenic Parliament (bill of the Ministry of Digital Governance)
instruments.current_status: Published in Government Gazette A' 114 of 20 July 2026; in force from publication (art. 58) unless individual provisions state otherwise. It replaces the AI chapter of Law 4961/2022.
instruments.summary: Greece's national implementing law for the EU AI Act (Part A, arts 1-26). It designates the Hellenic Data Protection Authority as market surveillance authority for prohibited practices, Annex III high-risk systems and Article 50 transparency obligations and as single point of contact, makes the Hellenic Telecommunications and Post Commission (EETT) the notifying authority with an AI Coordination and Know-how Centre and an AI regulatory sandbox (run with the HDPA), sets administrative sanctions and their publication, creates a mandatory register of AI systems used by public-sector bodies (declaration before deployment) and an AI Observatory in the Ministry of Digital Governance, and penalises removal of Article 50 deepfake/synthetic-content markings. Article 26 repeals Chapter B of Part A of Law 4961/2022 (the 2022 AI provisions); Article 47 separately allows an AI system to support state-aid evaluation under Law 4914/2022.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary national AI law: designates the AI Act competent authorities and sets national public-sector AI registration duties.

Formally a policy proposal of an advisory committee, with no separate government adoption act found; Law 5321/2026 (art. 22) refers to a 'National Strategy for AI' monitored by the AI Observatory without naming the document.
instruments.summary: Policy proposal for a national AI strategy prepared by the High-Level Advisory Committee on AI set up under the Prime Minister in November 2023 and chaired by Constantinos Daskalakis. The 154-page study sets guiding principles, six flagship programmes and recommendations on innovation and entrepreneurship, education and research, the regulatory framework, and AI in the state (health, defence, civil protection, culture, justice, revenue services and government efficiency).

instruments.english_title: Law 4961/2022 - Emerging information and communication technologies, strengthening digital governance and other provisions
instruments.issuing_authority: Hellenic Parliament (bill of the Ministry of Digital Governance)
instruments.current_status: Part A Chapter B (AI provisions) applied from 1 January 2023 (art. 116(2)) and was repealed by Article 26 of Law 5321/2026 from 20 July 2026. The other parts of the law (cybersecurity, IoT, unmanned aircraft, blockchain) remain in force.
instruments.summary: Law 4961/2022 (Gov. Gazette A' 146/27.07.2022) contained Greece's first AI rules in Part A, Chapter B (arts 3-14): public-sector bodies could use AI systems for decisions affecting rights only where a specific law provided for it, with an algorithmic impact assessment before deployment, transparency duties, obligations on AI contractors and a register of public-sector AI systems. Private employers had to inform workers before using AI systems affecting working conditions, and medium and large companies had to keep a register of their AI systems and an ethical data-use policy. It also set up a Coordinating Committee for AI, a Committee supervising the National AI Strategy and an AI Observatory; the rest of the law covers cybersecurity, IoT, drones and DLT.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Earlier national AI framework for public-sector and private-company AI use; its AI chapter was repealed by Law 5321/2026.

instruments.current_status: Published in Government Gazette B' 3804 of 17 July 2025; in force from publication.
instruments.summary: Joint decision no. 1961 creating a Special Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance reporting directly to the Minister of Digital Governance. Its mission is to design, coordinate and implement policies for AI use and data governance, coordinating bodies applying the national and EU AI and data framework, promoting responsible AI adoption and implementing national AI and data strategies. It sets up an AI Directorate (AI governance, AI standards and technological applications, AI regulatory compliance units) and a Data Governance Directorate.

instruments.english_title: Joint Ministerial Decision 55909/D6/2026 - Rules on the use of AI systems in the educational process and the protection of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministers of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports and of Digital Governance
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports
instruments.current_status: Signed 7 May 2026 and published in Government Gazette B' 2639 of 12 May 2026; in force from publication (art. 18).
instruments.summary: Joint ministerial decision setting binding conditions for the use of AI systems, including generative AI, in all secondary schools, in class and in distance learning. Use is voluntary for teachers and pupils after training and information; it bans fully automated assessment and profiling of pupils or teachers, AI use in written exams unless the teacher allows it, submitting work wholly or largely produced by AI, and unconsented deepfakes. It requires a data protection impact assessment before any system is used, names the Ministry of Education as controller, bars entering identifying personal data and requires annual awareness activities and teacher training.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector rule for AI in schools issued jointly by the education and digital ministries.

instruments.summary: Chapter A establishes 'Greek Artificial Intelligence Factory S.A.' (distinctive title 'PHAROS AI FACTORY'), a public-interest company supervised by the Minister of Digital Governance and a subsidiary of the Hellenic Corporation of Assets and Participations, to build an AI ecosystem in Greece by creating, supporting and using AI technologies and strengthening research, entrepreneurship and digital growth. instruments.current_status: Dated and digitally signed 22 September 2026 (ref. 34239 ΕΞ 2026); listed on the Special Secretariat's 'Resources' page (ai.gov.gr).
instruments.summary: Circular to ministries, secretariats, independent authorities, decentralised administrations and local authorities describing the European Commission's free multilingual AI services (translation, drafting, summarisation, transcription, anonymisation) available to public administrations. It asks bodies to use these tools responsibly: all generated texts, translations and summaries must be checked by staff, accuracy and suitability assessed case by case, and confidential or classified data must not be entered.

instruments.english_title: Hellenic Data Protection Authority Decision 35/2022 imposing a fine on Clearview AI, Inc.
instruments.current_status: Decision dated 13 July 2022 (ref. 1809). The HDPA publishes an anonymised English version (read) alongside the Greek original.
instruments.summary: Decision on a complaint by Homo Digitalis against the US facial-recognition company Clearview AI, whose service scrapes facial images from the internet into a biometric search database. The HDPA found breaches of the GDPR principles of lawfulness and transparency and of Articles 12, 14, 15 and 27, fined the company EUR 20 million, ordered it to answer the access request, banned it from collecting and processing personal data of people in Greece through its facial recognition methods and ordered deletion of such data already collected.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Leading Greek regulator enforcement decision on an AI (facial recognition) system.

leads.title: Υπουργικές αποφάσεις κατ' εξουσιοδότηση του ν. 5321/2026 (Μητρώο συστημάτων ΤΝ δημόσιου τομέα, ρυθμιστικό δοκιμαστήριο ΤΝ)
leads.english_title: Implementing ministerial decisions under Law 5321/2026 (public-sector AI systems register, AI regulatory sandbox)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Governance; Hellenic Telecommunications and Post Commission
leads.note: Law 5321/2026 art. 24 delegates detailed rules (register declarations, sandbox call by EETT under art. 12(3)); none found published in the gazette or on eett.gr / ai.gov.gr by 12 October 2026.

leads.title: Επικαιροποιημένο εθνικό σχέδιο / Εθνική Στρατηγική για την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη
leads.english_title: Updated national AI plan / National Strategy for AI
leads.issuing_authority: Special Secretariat for Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance
leads.note: ai.gov.gr ('Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη' page) says Greece is implementing and updating its national plan for the transition to the AI era, and Law 5321/2026 art. 22 refers to a National Strategy for AI; no separate adopted strategy document beyond the 2024 Blueprint was found.

leads.english_title: Ministry of Culture strategic plan on AI
leads.note: Ministerial speeches and releases on culture.gov.gr refer to an AI strategic plan and an NTUA agreement on AI for cultural heritage; only speeches/press material found, no plan document.
